beats.say: £2m: Richard Hammond's mansion paused for bats.
BBC says a survey found rare pipistrelle bats on the grounds.
The former Top Gear host bought the Georgian property near Abergavenny last November.
Plans for a padel court and a garage for his historic cars are on hold.
Hammond insists he will share the home with the protected species.

meta.summary: Richard Hammond's £2m Georgian mansion renovation in Wales has been paused after a survey discovered rare pipistrelle bats on the property. The presenter says he will find a way to share the home with them.
meta.comment: What would you do if bats moved into your dream home?
sources: BBC, Richard Hammond to 'find a way' to share mansion with bats after renovation plans paused
facts: Richard Hammond bought a 19th Century Georgian mansion in Llanwenarth near Abergavenny in November 2025.
Renovations including a padel court and car garage were paused after a survey found rare bats on the grounds.
Richard Hammond stated he will find a way of sharing his new home with the bats.
His new home is valued at £2m.
Renovation work was paused after a survey found several bat species including the common pipistrelle and soprano pipistrelles.
A new garage is planned to store Hammond's collection of historic and specialist vehicles.
